items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: We used to play a lot of the things that Nat Cole's group was playing... I'm out here doing this thing and aping Nat Cole... Nat Cole liked us very much

ctx.x: Yeah, I think Marjorie Hyams. And Chuck Wayne was the guitarist. At that time, Oscar Moore had just left Nat Cole's group, and he was with his brother's group. They had aa group called The Four Blazers, that featured Charlie Rouse.

items.q: Nat King Cole was at his peak then as far as the trio situation was concerned, and I liked the idea that the clubs were all using trios.

ctx.x: leave the band. He was quite disturbed. He said, "Whatever for? You're playing great, you're writing great" and the whole thing. I told him, "I really need to go home and study and learn." He said, "Man, you know enough. You should stay out here with the band." But I was convinced that I needed to know more.

So I quit the band and I came back to Washington. That was in September 1945. I came to Washington and formed a little trio. Incidentally, Tommy Potter left the band shortly after I did. When they came back, I formed this trio... Nat King Cole was at his peak then as far as the trio situation was concerned, and I liked the idea that the clubs were all using trios. There was a very good guitar player in Washington then whose name was Chester Brown. Chester and I had played together earlier in the Tommy Miles band.…

Anyway, I was very fortunate... When Tommy came back to Washington, I got Tommy and Chester, and we formed this trio. While I was forming the trio, one day I happened to get a call from Sarah Vaughan. She just called me to say hello. She says, "What are you doing?" I said, "I'm putting a trio together."
